title: Enforcement Decree of the Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Establishment of Master Plan, Etc.)
(1) "Cases of changing minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 6(2) of the Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means any of the following cases:
1. Where details concerning project implementation are changed to the extent that the purpose and direction of the master plan for the virtual convergence industry under Article 6(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as the "master plan") remain unchanged.
2. Where matters that do not affect the purpose and direction of the master plan and for which the grounds for change are clear are changed.
3. Where simple mistakes, clerical errors, omissions, or obvious errors are corrected.
(2) Where the master plan is finalized or changed pursuant to Article 6(2) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT shall announce its contents on the website of the Ministry of Science and ICT.
(3) Where an annual implementation plan under Article 6(4) of the Act is established or changed, the Minister of Science and ICT shall announce its contents on the website of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 3 (Scope of Fact-Finding Surveys, Etc.)
(1) The scope of a fact-finding survey under Article 8(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "fact-finding survey") shall be as follows:
1. The current state of the virtual convergence industry and virtual convergence business operators.
2. The current state of the use and dissemination of virtual convergence technology under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "virtual convergence technology").
3. The current state of the use and dissemination of virtual convergence services, etc. under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "virtual convergence services, etc.").
4. The current state of regulations relating to the virtual convergence industry.
5. The current state of personnel relating to the virtual convergence industry by gender, type of employment, and job, and forecasts of personnel demand.
6. The scale of research and development and investment relating to the virtual convergence industry.
7. The current state of exports relating to the virtual convergence industry.
8. Other matters concerning the current state of the virtual convergence industry, identification of tasks for regulatory improvement, etc.
(2) Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to conduct a fact-finding survey pursuant to Article 8(1) of the Act, the head shall establish criteria for selecting survey subjects and notify the survey subjects in advance of the survey plan, including the date, time, purpose, contents, etc. of the survey.
(3) Where requested to submit data or provide support pursuant to Article 8(2) of the Act, the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions"), business operators, enterprises, associations, research institutions, and others may submit data or provide support via information and communications networks or by electronic means such as email.

Article 4 (Persons Subject to Reporting of Virtual Convergence Platform Business)
"A person whose sales, etc. meet the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of Article 9(1) of the Act means a person whose sales from virtual convergence platform business in the immediately preceding fiscal year amounted to KRW 100 million or more.

Article 5 (Training of Specialized Personnel, Etc.)
(1) Where deemed necessary to establish policies for training specialized personnel under Article 10(1) of the Act, the head of a central administrative agency may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, or the heads of public institutions to submit data.
(2) Support under Article 10(2) of the Act shall cover the following:
1. Development of programs and teaching materials necessary for training specialized personnel.
2. Education and research necessary for training specialized personnel.
3. Identification and attraction of outstanding specialized personnel from overseas.
4. Other matters deemed necessary by the head of a central administrative agency for training specialized personnel.

Article 6 (Entrustment of Projects to Promote Technology Development)
(1) Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to entrust projects listed in the subparagraphs of Article 11(1) of the Act pursuant to paragraph (2) of the same Article, the head shall select the entity to be entrusted by comprehensively considering the personnel, facilities, equipment, level of expertise, and other relevant aspects of the institution or organization seeking entrustment.
(2) Where the head of a central administrative agency entrusts duties pursuant to Article 11(2) of the Act, the head shall publicly notify the institution or organization entrusted and the contents of the entrusted duties.

Article 7 (Support for Standardization)
(1) Where necessary to carry out the projects listed in the subparagraphs of Article 13(1) of the Act, the head of a central administrative agency may undertake the following support projects:
1. Projects to survey demand and establish standards strategies for standardization under the main clause of the introductory portion of Article 13(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as "standardization").
2. Projects to support verification of the conformity of virtual convergence services, etc. with standards, or the application or utilization of standards.
3. Projects to publicize standards.
4. Projects to train specialized personnel for standardization and promote exchanges and cooperation with specialized personnel at home and abroad.
5. Projects to survey and analyze trends in international standards and establish a framework for responding to them.
(2) Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to entrust duties concerning standardization pursuant to Article 13(3) of the Act, the head shall select the entity to be entrusted by comprehensively considering the personnel, expertise in standardization, and other relevant aspects of the institution or organization seeking entrustment.
(3) Where the head of a central administrative agency entrusts duties pursuant to Article 13(3) of the Act, the head shall publicly notify the institution or organization entrusted and the contents of the entrusted duties.

Article 8 (Designation of Dedicated Agencies, Etc.)
(1) Pursuant to Article 17(1) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT may designate as a dedicated agency (hereinafter referred to as a "dedicated agency") an institution or organization that meets all of the following requirements for designation:
1. It shall be an institution or organization falling under any of the following items:
(a) A public institution.
(b) An institution invested in or funded by a local government that has been designated and publicly notified pursuant to Article 5 of the Act on the Operation of Local Government-Invested or -Funded Institutions.
(c) Any other institution or organization established under the Civil Act or another Act that the Minister of Science and ICT recognizes as having expertise in promoting the virtual convergence industry.
2. It shall have a dedicated organizational unit and dedicated personnel necessary to perform the projects listed in the subparagraphs of Article 17(2) of the Act.
(2) "Projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17(2), subparagraph 6 of the Act means the following projects:
1. Projects to train specialized personnel for the virtual convergence industry.
2. Projects to support business start-ups in the virtual convergence industry.
3. Projects to support the identification and production of virtual convergence services, etc. and the promotion of their distribution.
4. Projects to expand opportunities to use virtual convergence services, etc.
5. Projects to improve the safety of virtual convergence services, etc.
6. Other projects deemed necessary by the Minister of Science and ICT to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(3) A dedicated agency designated pursuant to paragraph (1) shall establish detailed project plans and fund disbursement plans concerning the performance of the projects listed in the subparagraphs of Article 17(2) of the Act and submit them annually to the Minister of Science and ICT.
(4) Where the Minister of Science and ICT designates a dedicated agency pursuant to paragraph (1) or revokes the designation of a dedicated agency pursuant to Article 17(4) of the Act, the Minister shall announce that fact on the website of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 9 (Application for Authorization to Establish an Association)
(1) Where virtual convergence business operators intend to establish an association relating to the virtual convergence industry under Article 18(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "association"), at least 30 virtual convergence business operators shall act as promoters, prepare articles of incorporation, and apply to the Minister of Science and ICT for authorization following a resolution of the general meeting of promoters.
(2) A person who intends to apply for authorization under paragraph (1) shall submit to the Minister of Science and ICT an application for authorization of establishment prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by the following documents:
1. Articles of incorporation;
2. A list of promoters and their curricula vitae;
3. Written consents to assume office as officers;
4. A business plan and a plan for budgetary revenue and expenditure.

Article 10 (Designation of Regional Virtual Convergence Industry Support Centers, Etc.)
(1) A person who intends to obtain designation as a regional virtual convergence industry support center under Article 19(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "support center") shall meet all of the following requirements:
1. The person shall be a nonprofit corporation established under Article 32 of the Civil Act;
2. The person shall have secured the specialized department, personnel, facilities, and equipment necessary to perform the projects under Article 19(2) of the Act.
(2) Detailed criteria for the designation requirements for support centers under paragraph (1), subparagraph 2, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.
(3) A person who intends to obtain designation as a support center under Article 19(1) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of Science and ICT an application for designation prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by the following documents:
1. Articles of incorporation or equivalent business operating regulations;
2. A business plan;
3. A statement of the current status of specialized personnel and a personnel deployment plan;
4. A statement of facilities;
5. An organizational chart specifying the system for performing duties;
6. A list of work performed in the virtual convergence industry over the preceding three years (only where such work has been performed).
(4) Where a person who has applied for designation under paragraph (3) meets all the requirements under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT may designate that person as a support center.
(5) Where the Minister of Science and ICT designates a support center under paragraph (4), the Minister shall issue to the applicant a support center designation certificate prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT.
(6) A person designated as a support center under paragraph (4) shall submit the business plan for the relevant year to the Minister of Science and ICT by January 31 each year.
(7) Where the Minister of Science and ICT designates a support center under paragraph (4), or revokes its designation or orders suspension of its operations under Article 19(4) of the Act, the Minister shall publicly announce that fact on the website of the Ministry of Science and ICT.
(8) The criteria for revocation of designation and suspension of operations of support centers under Article 19(4) of the Act shall be as set out in the Annex.

Article 11 (Support for Virtual Convergence Business Operators)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 4 of Article 20(1) of the Act means the following matters:
1. Provision of information and counseling concerning funds, personnel, technology, and other resources;
2. Provision of space necessary for business operations;
3. Support for promoting distribution, such as publicity, promotion of purchases, and development of sales channels for virtual convergence services, etc.;
4. Other matters that the head of a central administrative agency or the head of a local government deems necessary to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(2) When providing support under Article 20(1) of the Act, the heads of central administrative agencies and local governments may give priority to virtual convergence business operators that qualify as small and medium enterprises under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises.

Article 12 (Implementation of Pilot Projects, Etc.)
(1) Where the heads of central administrative agencies and local governments intend to implement a pilot project under Article 22(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "pilot project"), they shall formulate a pilot project implementation plan that includes the following matters:
1. The purpose and implementation structure of the pilot project;
2. The virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. to be applied in the pilot project;
3. The implementation period of the pilot project;
4. Arrangements for raising the funds necessary to implement the pilot project;
5. Other matters necessary for the smooth implementation of the pilot project.
(2) The heads of central administrative agencies and local governments may provide the following support to persons participating in pilot projects under Article 22(2) of the Act:
1. Establishment of the infrastructure necessary for efficient performance of the pilot project;
2. Financial support necessary to perform the pilot project;
3. Other matters deemed necessary to achieve the purpose of the pilot project.
(3) The heads of central administrative agencies and local governments shall, under Article 22(3) of the Act, evaluate the performance of a pilot project, including the record of utilization and spillover effects of the virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc., within one year from the date the pilot project ends.

Article 13 (Virtual Convergence Project Impact Assessment)
(1) "Institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 26(1) of the Act means the following institutions:
1. Central administrative agencies;
2. Local governments;
3. Public institutions;
4. Local public corporations and local public agencies established under the Local Public Enterprises Act.
(2) The heads of the institutions listed in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "central administrative agencies, etc.") shall examine the following matters when conducting a virtual convergence project impact assessment under the main clause of Article 26(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as a "virtual convergence project impact assessment"):
1. Similarity between the virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. associated with the relevant virtual convergence project (meaning a virtual convergence project under the main clause of Article 26(1) of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article) and the virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. of the private sector;
2. The possibility that the relevant virtual convergence project will encroach on the private-sector market;
3. The necessity and public nature of the relevant virtual convergence project.
(3) Based on the results of the virtual convergence project impact assessment, the heads of central administrative agencies, etc. shall prepare a report on the results of the virtual convergence project impact assessment in accordance with detailed assessment items determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT, and submit the report to the Minister of Science and ICT.
(4) Where the heads of central administrative agencies, etc. have conducted a virtual convergence project impact assessment, they shall publicly announce the report on the results of the virtual convergence project impact assessment under paragraph (3) on their websites no later than five days before the date of the tender announcement for implementing the relevant virtual convergence project. However, in urgent cases, the report may be publicly announced no later than three days before the date of the tender announcement.
(5) Where, as a result of the virtual convergence project impact assessment, it is determined that proceeding with the relevant virtual convergence project is inappropriate, the heads of central administrative agencies, etc. shall reconsider that project and either adjust its content or discontinue its implementation.
(6) "Virtual convergence projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 26(1) of the Act means the following projects:
1. Pilot projects;
2. Projects for which a software project impact assessment under the main clause of Article 43(1) of the Software Promotion Act has been conducted;
3. Virtual convergence projects relating to fields such as national security, public security, and foreign affairs for which provision of services by the private sector is inappropriate;
4. Other virtual convergence projects that the Minister of Science and ICT, in view of their impact on the private-sector market, deems not to require a virtual convergence project impact assessment and publicly notifies as such.
(7) Matters necessary for virtual convergence project impact assessments, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (6), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT.

Article 14 (Proposals for Temporary Standards)
(1) Where necessary to review whether temporary standards under Article 28 (1) of the Act need to be established, the Minister of Science and ICT may request the head of a relevant central administrative agency, the head of a local government, or the head of a public institution to provide necessary materials. In such cases, the head of the institution receiving the request shall cooperate unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(2) Where the Minister of Science and ICT deems it necessary to supplement an application for temporary standards submitted pursuant to Article 28 (2) of the Act, the Minister may set a period and require the applicant to supplement the application within that period.
(3) Upon receiving an application for temporary standards pursuant to Article 28 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT shall notify the applicant of the results of the review within 30 days after receiving the application (excluding the period required for supplementation under paragraph (2)).

Article 15 (Matters to Consider When Establishing Temporary Standards)
When establishing or revising temporary standards pursuant to the proviso to Article 28 (1) or the main clause of Article 28 (3) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall consider the following matters:
1. The effects of the temporary standards on the virtual convergence industry and related industries;
2. The effects of the temporary standards on user convenience and safety.

Article 16 (Procedures for Establishing Temporary Standards)
(1) When establishing or revising temporary standards pursuant to the proviso to Article 28 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT shall hear the opinions of virtual convergence business operators, relevant institutions and organizations, and experts concerning the contents of the temporary standards.
(2) When establishing or revising temporary standards pursuant to the main clause of Article 28 (3) of the Act, the head of a relevant central administrative agency shall consult with the Minister of Science and ICT and hear the opinions of virtual convergence business operators, relevant institutions and organizations, and experts concerning the contents of the temporary standards.
(3) Where necessary to establish or revise temporary standards under the proviso to Article 28 (1) or the main clause of Article 28 (3) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may request the head of a relevant central administrative agency, the head of a local government, or the head of a public institution to provide necessary materials. In such cases, the head of the institution receiving the request shall cooperate unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 17 (Entrustment of Duties)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may entrust the following duties to an institution or organization listed in any subparagraph of paragraph (2), pursuant to Article 33 (2) of the Act:
1. Conducting fact-finding surveys under Article 8 of the Act;
2. Receiving reports and reports of changes concerning virtual convergence platform businesses under Article 9 of the Act, requiring supplementation, and issuing certificates of receipt of reports;
3. Supporting virtual convergence project impact assessments under Article 26 of the Act;
4. Reviewing proposals and requesting the establishment or revision of temporary standards under Article 28 (1) of the Act;
5. The following duties concerning the designation of support centers under Article 10:
  (a) Receiving applications for designation as a support center and confirming the contents of the applications under Article 10 (3);
  (b) Issuing certificates of designation as a support center under Article 10 (5) (meaning certificates of designation as a support center issued in the name of the Minister of Science and ICT);
  (c) Confirming whether grounds for revocation of the designation of a support center or suspension of its operations under Article 10 (8) exist.
(2) Institutions or organizations to which duties may be entrusted under paragraph (1) are as follows:
1. Dedicated agencies;
2. Associations;
3. Other institutions or organizations that the Minister of Science and ICT recognizes as having expertise in duties concerning promotion of the virtual convergence industry and specifies by public notice.
(3) Where the Minister of Science and ICT entrusts duties under paragraph (1), the Minister shall publicly notify the institution or organization entrusted with the duties and the contents of the entrusted duties.

Article 18 (Review of Regulations)
The Minister of Science and ICT shall review the appropriateness of each of the following matters every three years, with January 1, 2024 as the reference date (meaning before the day corresponding to the reference date in every third year), and take measures for improvement or other necessary measures:
1. Persons subject to reporting of virtual convergence platform businesses under Article 4;
2. Requirements for designation of dedicated agencies under Article 8 (1);
3. Requirements for designation of support centers under Article 10 (1);
4. Criteria for revocation of the designation of support centers and suspension of their operations under Article 10 (8) and the Annex.

ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 34853, August 27, 2024>

This Decree shall enter into force on August 28, 2024.
